candidate_relations.reason: Schwannoma is the reference diagnosis for this long-standing cystic supraclavicular mass.
Thyroglossal duct cysts are midline; this is a lateral supraclavicular cystic mass.
Ultrasound/FNA suggested branchial cleft cyst, a different developmental cyst from schwannoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Branchial cleft cyst as the preoperative misdiagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: Neurogenic tumor is the parent family of schwannoma and lacks schwannoma specificity.
Epidermoid cyst is a keratinous cyst, not a nerve-sheath tumor.
There is no fever or systemic illness to support tuberculous lymphadenitis.
Cystic schwannoma is the same schwannoma with the cystic/septated morphology shown on ultrasound.
Seroma follows surgery/trauma, which is denied.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Seroma versus chronic mass without trauma

candidate_relations.reason: Cystic hygroma/lymphangioma is a lymphatic malformation, typically pediatric, not schwannoma.
Hemangioma is a vascular tumor, not a neurogenic cystic mass.
Lipoma is solid fat, not a septated cystic mass.
Dermoid cyst is a germ-cell/cutaneous inclusion cyst, not schwannoma.
Neurilemmoma is synonymous with schwannoma.
Thymic cysts are mediastinal/thymic, not a superficial lateral supraclavicular mass.
Soft-tissue tumor is a generic parent and omits schwannoma.
No trauma and a six-year painless course exclude hematoma.
Sarcoidosis does not present as this isolated cystic lateral neck mass.
A six-year indolent mobile mass without systemic cancer is not lymph-node metastasis.
Nerve-sheath tumor includes schwannoma and neurofibroma and lacks schwannoma specificity.
Plunging ranula is a sublingual extravasation cyst, not a supraclavicular nerve-sheath tumor.

case_quality_flags: Preoperative imaging was interpreted as branchial cleft cyst; reference histology is schwannoma.
